newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- flat, focus on heavy calendar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- flat, focus on heavy calendar.

text.p: U.S. municipal prices were unchanged at midday, recovering from early weakness attributed to the week's heavy new issue calendar, traders said.
"You have a very cautious muni cash market," one trader said. "We're probably even on the day after being down 1/8 to 1/4. I think we're waiting for the calendar this week."
Lehman Brothers said Monday it would price the week's largest negotiated offering on Thursday, a $640 million Arapahoe County, Colo., deal for the E-470 Public Highway project.
The deal, which will carry insurance from MBIA Insurance Corp, is the largest of the $3.6 billion in deals expected for the week, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $2.6 billion in 52 sales.
On the competitive side, 52 sales totaling $966 million were scheduled. A $250 million Maryland offering on Wednesday was the largest.
Muni traders said a stronger government market was helping municipal prices avoid losses from supply pressure.

The government long bond was up 14/32 at 102-21/32, pushing the yield down to 6.42 percent. Analysts attributed gains there in part to a stronger dollar, but said activity in the government market was light ahead of the week's indicators.

Among the week's more closely-watched data will be the Employment Cost Index, a key indicator of inflation, which was set for release Tuesday. Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the figure to show a 0.8 percent increase.

The week's other main focus, the payrolls data for July, were due out Friday. Predictions are for a 193,000 rise, down from the previous month's 217,000. The unemployment rate was predicted at 4.9 percent, down from 5.0 percent.

In Chicago futures markets Monday, September municipal bonds rose 6/32 to 120-28/32, while September Treasury bonds gained 10/32 to 115-11/32. The MOB sread between the two contracts narrowed to 177 ticks from 181 ticks at the close on Friday.
In the secondary market, bids on Atlanta FGIC 5-1/4 water and sewer bonds of 2027 were unchanged at 5.37 percent.
Florida Ports Financing Commission MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 were bid at 5.49 percent, one basis point below Friday's closing bid.
